correctness.rationale: A side of a rank-(n−2) diagram has exactly two omitted vertices: they can be singletons for any pair, or a hook for an adjacent pair, because a hook enclosing a propagating vertex would violate planarity. The other vertices match in increasing order, so either outer side is free, with W_n choices each. For disjoint inner omitted sets all four omitted vertices carry a boundary connection, and any hook joins stubs on the same side, leaving rank n−4 and no floating component. The three ordered counts with zero, one, and two hooks are respectively C(n,2)C(n−2,2), 2(n−1)C(n−2,2), and (n−2)(n−3). With one common vertex the no-hook, one-hook, and two-hook cases give counts n(n−1)(n−2), 4(n−1)(n−2), and 2(n−2): the common vertex floats only without hooks, and two overlapping hooks give exactly one new opposite-boundary connection. With coinciding sets there are two isolated paths, one hooked path, or a two-edge loop, with counts C(n,2), 2(n−1), and n−1. This yields all seven coefficients after the free factor W_n². The disjoint case cannot occur at n=3, so omit its term. The loop event has exactly n−1 inner pairs out of W_n², consistent with the reported probability and total mass W_n⁴.
residual_risks: The finite reproductions are comparisons, not the all-n proof. The loop convention retains the two parallel hook edges as a middle loop; isolated vertices are zero-length paths.

value.rationale: The first rank class allowing both singleton omissions and hooks gives a natural product census that distinguishes loss of rank from the creation of floating paths and loops. The exact joint law, including the rank-preserving overlap of distinct hooks, is useful for random product calculations and evaluating rank-refined class sums in weighted multiplication. Those outcomes are not available from diagram-class dimensions alone.
residual_risks: This is not an individual output-fiber theorem, a count for other ranks, or a complete set of structure constants.
